poc_summary: JS shell script: create a 1MB ArrayBuffer `a`, build a Proxy `b` whose `get` trap (triggered when FeatureOptions::init reads the 'builtins' property) calls `a.transfer(unescape)` to detach `a`'s backing buffer; then call `WebAssembly.validate(a, b)`. The compile-options parsing causes a.transfer() to free the ArrayBuffer's data while WasmJS.cpp still holds a raw pointer into it from GetBufferSource(), so subsequent bytecode decoding reads freed memory.
explanation: Reproduced by running `/work/obj-verify-js/dist/bin/js /poc/poc.js` (the ASan-instrumented js shell) identically across all three built revisions. post_intro (commit 75fa8115ffad): crashes with exit 134, AddressSanitizer reports 'heap-use-after-free on address ... READ of size 4' in js::wasm::Decoder::read<unsigned int> / readFixedU32 / DecodePreamble / DecodeModuleEnvironment / Validate / WebAssembly_validate (js/src/wasm/WasmValidate.cpp, WasmJS.cpp) -- exactly the code path and bug_type (UseAfterFree) described in the report: GetBufferSource() captures a raw non-owning pointer into the ArrayBuffer before FeatureOptions::init runs arbitrary JS (the Proxy get-trap) that detaches/frees the buffer via ArrayBuffer.prototype.transfer, leaving a dangling pointer used by the decoder. pre_intro (commit 92c3bbb32a85, before the regressing refactor) and post_benign (companion fix applied on top of the same parent) both run the identical script and command to completion with exit 0 and no sanitizer report, confirming the UAF window did not exist before introduction and is closed by the benign/fix commit. No ambiguity: build succeeded cleanly for all three versions, the same PoC/input/command was used throughout, and the ASan report names the exact affected file/function from meta.json's root_cause and findings.
